questions.subject: Physical Education
questions.text: Ancient Greece is historically significant to the development of Physical Education mainly for its
options: creation of the first modern gymnasium equipment
development of the modern marathon distance
establishment of the ancient Olympic Games and emphasis on physical training
questions.explanation: Ancient Greece is historically significant for establishing the ancient Olympic Games and placing strong cultural emphasis on physical training and athleticism.

questions.subject: Physical Education
questions.text: The industrial era in Europe influenced the development of Physical Education partly through
options: the complete elimination of all physical activity from daily life
the abolition of all organised sport
growing concern for workers' physical fitness and the rise of organised school physical training
the invention of the ancient Olympic Games
questions.explanation: Industrial-era Europe saw growing concern for public health and fitness, contributing to the rise of organised physical training programmes in schools.

questions.subject: Physical Education
questions.text: The development of modern Nigerian sports history has been shaped significantly by
options: the exclusive practice of ancient Greek sports
isolation from all international sporting events
a complete absence of any organised sporting activity
the growth of organised school sports, national competitions, and international participation
questions.explanation: Modern Nigerian sports history reflects the growth of organised school and national competitions, alongside increasing participation in international sporting events.

questions.subject: Physical Education
questions.text: The cognitive domain of Physical Education's developmental goals is primarily concerned with
options: knowledge and understanding of rules, strategies, and health concepts
questions.explanation: The cognitive domain focuses on developing knowledge and understanding, such as learning rules, strategies, and health-related concepts.

questions.subject: Physical Education
questions.text: The affective domain of Physical Education's developmental goals is primarily concerned with
options: attitudes, values, sportsmanship, and social/emotional development
questions.explanation: The affective domain addresses attitudes, values, and social-emotional development, including qualities like sportsmanship and teamwork.

questions.subject: Physical Education
questions.text: The psychomotor domain of Physical Education's developmental goals is primarily concerned with
options: the development of physical skills and movement abilities
purely theoretical knowledge with no physical component
attitudes and values alone, with no skill development
questions.explanation: The psychomotor domain focuses on developing physical skills and movement abilities through practice and physical activity.

questions.subject: Physical Education
questions.text: The health-related fitness component describing the heart and lungs' ability to supply oxygen during sustained physical activity is called
questions.explanation: Cardiovascular endurance measures the efficiency of the heart and lungs in supplying oxygen to muscles during sustained physical activity.

questions.subject: Physical Education
questions.text: The health-related fitness component describing the maximum force a muscle or muscle group can exert in a single effort is called
questions.explanation: Muscular strength refers to the maximum force a muscle or muscle group can generate in a single maximal effort.

questions.subject: Physical Education
questions.text: The health-related fitness component describing a muscle's ability to perform repeated contractions over an extended period without fatigue is called
questions.explanation: Muscular endurance measures a muscle's ability to sustain repeated contractions over time without becoming fatigued.

questions.subject: Physical Education
questions.text: The health-related fitness component describing the range of motion available at a joint or group of joints is called
questions.explanation: Flexibility refers to the range of motion possible at a joint, influenced by factors such as muscle and connective tissue elasticity.

questions.subject: Physical Education
questions.text: The health-related fitness component describing the relative proportion of fat, muscle, bone, and other tissues making up the body is called
questions.explanation: Body composition describes the relative proportions of fat mass, muscle mass, bone, and other tissues that make up total body weight.

questions.subject: Physical Education
questions.text: The skill-related fitness component describing the ability to rapidly change body position or direction with control is called
questions.explanation: Agility refers to the ability to quickly and accurately change body direction or position while maintaining control.

questions.subject: Physical Education
questions.text: The skill-related fitness component describing the ability to maintain body equilibrium, whether stationary or moving, is called
questions.explanation: Balance describes the ability to maintain the body's equilibrium, whether in a static position or while in motion.

questions.subject: Physical Education
questions.text: The skill-related fitness component describing the ability to use the senses together with body parts to perform smooth, accurate movements is called
questions.explanation: Coordination involves integrating sensory information with motor skills to execute smooth, accurate, and well-timed movements.

questions.subject: Physical Education
questions.text: The skill-related fitness component describing the ability to exert maximum force in the shortest possible time is called
questions.explanation: Power combines strength and speed, describing the ability to exert maximum force in the shortest possible time.

questions.subject: Physical Education
questions.text: The skill-related fitness component describing the time elapsed between a stimulus and the beginning of a response to it is called
questions.explanation: Reaction time measures how quickly an individual responds to a given stimulus, an important factor in many competitive sports.

questions.subject: Physical Education
questions.text: The skill-related fitness component describing the ability to move the body (or part of it) from one point to another in the shortest possible time is called
questions.explanation: Speed refers to the ability to move quickly from one point to another, a key skill-related fitness component in many sports.

questions.subject: Physical Education
questions.text: A standard test used to assess cardiovascular endurance, requiring participants to run as far as possible within a set time, is the
questions.explanation: The Cooper 12-minute run test measures the maximum distance covered in twelve minutes, providing an estimate of cardiovascular endurance.

questions.subject: Physical Education
questions.text: A standard test used to assess flexibility, typically measuring how far a person can reach forward from a seated position, is the
questions.explanation: The sit-and-reach test measures flexibility, particularly of the lower back and hamstrings, by assessing forward reach from a seated position.

questions.subject: Physical Education
questions.text: A standard test used to assess power in the legs, measuring the height a person can jump vertically from a standing position, is the
questions.explanation: The vertical jump test measures leg power by assessing the maximum height a person can jump vertically from a standing start.

questions.subject: Physical Education
questions.text: The starting position used by sprinters, involving hands and feet positioned on the track with the aid of starting blocks, is called the
questions.explanation: The crouch start, aided by starting blocks, allows sprinters to generate maximum explosive power at the beginning of a race.

questions.subject: Physical Education
questions.text: In sprinting, the phase immediately following the start, during which a runner builds up to maximum speed, is called
questions.explanation: Acceleration is the phase where a sprinter progressively builds speed from the start until reaching their maximum velocity.

questions.subject: Physical Education
questions.text: A technique used by sprinters at the finish line, leaning the torso forward to cross the line slightly sooner, is called the
questions.explanation: The lean (or dip) finish involves leaning the torso forward at the finish line, helping a sprinter's torso cross marginally sooner in a close race.

questions.subject: Physical Education
questions.text: Races covering distances such as 800m and 1500m, requiring a balance of speed and endurance, are classified as
questions.explanation: Middle-distance events, such as the 800m and 1500m, require athletes to balance elements of both speed and endurance.

questions.subject: Physical Education
questions.text: Races covering longer distances, such as 5000m, 10000m, and the marathon, are classified as
questions.explanation: Long-distance events, such as the 5000m, 10000m, and marathon, place heavy emphasis on sustained aerobic endurance.

questions.subject: Physical Education
questions.text: A track event in which athletes must clear a series of barriers while running is called
questions.explanation: Hurdling requires athletes to clear a series of fixed barriers at speed while maintaining running rhythm and technique.

questions.subject: Physical Education
questions.text: A track event in which a team of runners each complete a portion of the total distance, passing a baton between them, is called
questions.explanation: Relay racing involves a team of athletes, each running a set distance (leg) and passing a baton to the next runner.

questions.subject: Physical Education
questions.text: In relay racing, a baton exchange in which the receiving runner watches the baton being passed into their hand is called a
questions.explanation: A visual baton exchange involves the receiving athlete watching the baton as it is passed, often used in shorter relays where precision is critical.

questions.subject: Physical Education
questions.text: In relay racing, a baton exchange in which the receiving runner does not look back, instead reaching back to receive the baton based on timing and practice, is called a
questions.explanation: A non-visual (blind) exchange relies on practised timing rather than sight, allowing the receiving runner to maintain forward speed and focus.

questions.subject: Physical Education
questions.text: A jumping technique in the long jump involving a cycling leg motion in the air to maintain balance before landing is called the
questions.explanation: The hitch-kick technique involves a cycling leg motion during flight, helping the long jumper maintain balance and extend their jump distance.

questions.subject: Physical Education
questions.text: A simpler long jump technique in which the jumper holds a fixed body position through the air before landing is called the
questions.explanation: The sail style is a simpler long jump technique in which the body maintains a relatively fixed position throughout the flight phase.

questions.subject: Physical Education
questions.text: A field event involving a hop, step, and jump performed in sequence to achieve maximum distance is called the
questions.explanation: The triple jump requires an athlete to perform a hop, a step, and a jump in sequence, aiming for maximum combined distance.

questions.subject: Physical Education
questions.text: A high jump technique, now the dominant style, involving the athlete going over the bar backward and head-first is called the
questions.explanation: The Fosbury flop, now the standard technique in competitive high jump, involves clearing the bar backward and head-first.

questions.subject: Physical Education
questions.text: An older high jump technique in which the athlete rolls over the bar facing downward, largely replaced by the Fosbury flop, is called the
questions.explanation: The Western roll was an earlier high jump technique, largely superseded by the more efficient Fosbury flop in competitive athletics.

questions.subject: Physical Education
questions.text: A shot put technique involving a linear, gliding movement across the throwing circle before release is called the
questions.explanation: The O'Brien glide technique uses a linear gliding movement across the circle to build momentum before the shot is released.

questions.subject: Physical Education
questions.text: A shot put technique involving a spinning, rotational movement across the throwing circle before release, similar in style to discus throwing, is called the
questions.explanation: The rotational shot put technique uses a spinning motion across the circle to generate momentum, resembling the discus throwing technique.

questions.subject: Physical Education
questions.text: A field event involving throwing a heavy, flat, disc-shaped implement for maximum distance is called the
questions.explanation: The discus throw requires an athlete to throw a flat, disc-shaped implement for maximum distance, using a rotational technique.

questions.subject: Physical Education
questions.text: A field event involving throwing a long, spear-like implement for maximum distance is called the
questions.explanation: The javelin throw requires an athlete to throw a long, spear-shaped implement, using a running approach to generate momentum before release.

questions.subject: Physical Education
questions.text: A field event involving throwing a heavy metal ball attached to a wire and handle, using a spinning technique for momentum, is called the
questions.explanation: The hammer throw involves spinning to generate momentum before releasing a heavy metal ball attached to a wire and handle.

questions.subject: Physical Education
questions.text: The official responsible for determining the order of finish in a track race is called the
questions.explanation: Track judges are responsible for observing and determining the correct order of finish among competing athletes.

questions.subject: Physical Education
questions.text: The official responsible for recording the exact time taken by each athlete to complete a race is called the
questions.explanation: Timekeepers use stopwatches or automated timing systems to accurately record each athlete's race completion time.

questions.subject: Physical Education
questions.text: The official responsible for signalling the beginning of a race, typically using a starting gun or similar device, is called the
questions.explanation: The starter signals the official beginning of a race, ensuring a fair and synchronised start for all competing athletes.

questions.subject: Physical Education
questions.text: The official responsible for overseeing rules compliance and resolving disputes within field events is called the
questions.explanation: Field referees oversee rule compliance and resolve disputes specifically within field events, such as jumps and throws.

questions.subject: Physical Education
questions.text: The official responsible for measuring wind speed and direction during sprint and jump events, since excessive tailwinds can affect record validity, is called the
questions.explanation: The wind gauge operator measures wind conditions during relevant events, since excessive tailwind can invalidate a performance for record purposes.

questions.subject: Physical Education
questions.text: A standard outdoor athletics track is typically measured as
questions.explanation: A standard outdoor athletics track measures 400 metres for one complete lap, the basis for many middle- and long-distance race distances.

questions.subject: Physical Education
questions.text: In a 4 x 100m relay race, each of the four team members runs a distance of
questions.explanation: In a 4 x 100m relay, each of the four runners on a team covers a distance of 100 metres before passing the baton.

questions.subject: Physical Education
questions.text: A common rule in relay racing requires the baton exchange to occur within a designated
questions.explanation: Relay racing rules require the baton to be passed within a specific marked takeover (changeover) zone on the track.

questions.subject: Physical Education
questions.text: In the long jump, a competitor's jump is measured from the take-off board to the
options: farthest mark made in the sand
nearest mark made in the sand by any part of the body
centre of the sand pit regardless of the landing
questions.explanation: Long jump distances are measured from the take-off board to the nearest mark left in the sand pit by any part of the athlete's body.

questions.subject: Physical Education
questions.text: In the high jump, a competitor is eliminated from further attempts at a given height after
options: three consecutive failed attempts at that height
questions.explanation: In competitive high jump, an athlete is eliminated from further attempts at a given height after three consecutive failures.

questions.subject: Physical Education
questions.text: A team sport played on a rectangular pitch, using a spherical ball, primarily kicked (with limited handling except by the goalkeeper), is called
questions.explanation: Football (soccer) is played on a rectangular pitch, with players primarily using their feet to control and pass the ball, except for the goalkeeper.

questions.subject: Physical Education
questions.text: A team sport played on an indoor court, in which players score by shooting a ball through an elevated hoop, is called
questions.explanation: Basketball involves shooting a ball through an elevated hoop to score points, typically played on an indoor court.

questions.subject: Physical Education
questions.text: A team sport played across a net, in which players strike the ball to keep it airborne and grounded only on the opponent's side, is called
questions.explanation: Volleyball requires teams to hit the ball over a net, aiming to ground it on the opponent's side while preventing it from touching their own.

questions.subject: Physical Education
questions.text: A team sport in which players use their hands to throw a ball into a goal, combining elements of basketball and football, is called
questions.explanation: Handball combines elements of basketball and football, with players using their hands to pass and throw the ball into the opposing goal.

questions.subject: Physical Education
questions.text: A team sport played with curved sticks, in which players manoeuvre a small ball into the opposing team's goal, is called
questions.explanation: Hockey is played using curved sticks to control and manoeuvre a small ball, with the aim of scoring in the opponent's goal.

questions.subject: Physical Education
questions.text: A racket sport played on a court divided by a net, using a ball that bounces, played as singles or doubles, is called
questions.explanation: Lawn tennis is played on a court divided by a net, with players using rackets to strike a bouncing ball, competing as singles or doubles.

questions.subject: Physical Education
questions.text: A racket sport played on a small table divided by a low net, using a lightweight ball, is called
questions.explanation: Table tennis is played on a small table divided by a low net, using paddles to strike a lightweight ball back and forth.

questions.subject: Physical Education
questions.text: A racket sport played with a lightweight, feathered projectile called a shuttlecock, hit over a net, is called
questions.explanation: Badminton uses a lightweight shuttlecock, struck with rackets over a net, rather than a bouncing ball as in tennis or table tennis.

questions.subject: Physical Education
questions.text: A bat-and-ball sport played between two teams, involving bowling, batting, and fielding on a large oval-shaped field, is called
questions.explanation: Cricket is a bat-and-ball sport involving bowling, batting, and fielding, played between two teams on a large field with a central pitch.

questions.subject: Physical Education
questions.text: A gymnastics activity performed on a padded floor area, involving skills such as rolls, cartwheels, and handstands, is generally classified as
questions.explanation: Floor activities (tumbling) are performed on a padded surface, involving skills such as rolls, cartwheels, and handstands, without additional apparatus.

questions.subject: Physical Education
questions.text: A basic gymnastics skill involving rolling forward along the floor, tucking the body to rotate smoothly, is called a
questions.explanation: A forward roll involves tucking the body and rolling smoothly forward along the floor, a foundational gymnastics skill.

questions.subject: Physical Education
questions.text: A basic gymnastics skill involving rolling backward along the floor, similar in technique to a forward roll but in reverse, is called a
questions.explanation: A backward roll mirrors the forward roll technique, but performed by rolling backward along the floor.

questions.subject: Physical Education
questions.text: A gymnastics skill in which the body rotates sideways, passing through a momentary handstand position with legs extended outward, is called a
questions.explanation: A cartwheel involves a sideways rotation of the body, passing through a brief handstand-like position with the legs extended in a wide 'star' shape.

questions.subject: Physical Education
questions.text: A gymnastics skill in which the body is supported upside down by the hands alone, with the body extended vertically, is called a
questions.explanation: A handstand involves supporting the entire body upside down using only the hands, with the body extended vertically in balance.

questions.subject: Physical Education
questions.text: A gymnastics skill in which the body is supported upside down primarily by the head and hands together, is called a
questions.explanation: A headstand involves supporting the body upside down using the head and hands together as a stable tripod base.

questions.subject: Physical Education
questions.text: Gymnastics activities that involve using specific pieces of equipment, such as vaulting boxes and parallel bars, are generally classified as
questions.explanation: Apparatus activities involve gymnastics skills performed using specific equipment, distinguishing them from floor-only tumbling activities.

questions.subject: Physical Education
questions.text: A gymnastics apparatus event involving a run-up and jump over a raised, padded box-like structure is called
questions.explanation: Vaulting involves a running approach followed by a jump over a raised, padded vaulting box or table apparatus.

questions.subject: Physical Education
questions.text: A gymnastics apparatus consisting of two horizontal bars set at the same height, used for swinging and balancing skills, is called the
questions.explanation: Parallel bars consist of two horizontal bars at the same height, used by gymnasts to perform swinging, balancing, and strength-based skills.

questions.subject: Physical Education
questions.text: A gymnastics apparatus consisting of a narrow, elevated beam requiring balance and precision for various skills, is called the
questions.explanation: The balance beam is a narrow, elevated apparatus requiring precise balance and control as gymnasts perform routines along its length.

questions.subject: Physical Education
questions.text: A gymnastics apparatus resembling a padded horse-like structure with handles, on which gymnasts perform circular and swinging leg movements, is called the
questions.explanation: The pommel horse is a padded apparatus with handles, on which gymnasts perform circular and swinging leg movements while supporting themselves with their hands.

questions.subject: Physical Education
questions.text: In football (soccer), the standard number of players on the field per team, including the goalkeeper, is
questions.explanation: Football (soccer) is played with 11 players per team on the field, including the goalkeeper.

questions.subject: Physical Education
questions.text: In basketball, the standard number of players on the court per team at any one time is
questions.explanation: Basketball is played with 5 players per team on the court at any given time.

questions.subject: Physical Education
questions.text: In volleyball, the standard number of players on the court per team at any one time is
questions.explanation: Volleyball is typically played with 6 players per team on the court at any given time.

questions.subject: Physical Education
questions.text: In football (soccer), a player is penalised with an indirect or direct free kick, or in some cases a caution, for committing a
questions.explanation: A foul in football refers to an illegal action by a player, such as tripping or handling the ball, resulting in a free kick or other penalty for the opposing team.

questions.subject: Physical Education
questions.text: In basketball, the act of illegally moving with the ball without dribbling it is called
questions.explanation: Travelling is a basketball violation in which a player moves their pivot foot illegally while holding the ball without dribbling.

questions.subject: Physical Education
questions.text: In basketball, points scored from a successful shot taken from beyond the marked arc are worth
questions.explanation: A successful shot taken from beyond the three-point arc is worth three points in basketball, more than the standard two-point field goal.

questions.subject: Physical Education
questions.text: A key tactical skill in football (soccer) involves players creating and using open space through movement and
options: avoiding all forms of ball possession
standing completely still throughout the match
questions.explanation: Effective football tactics rely on players moving to create space and using accurate passing to maintain possession and create scoring opportunities.

questions.subject: Physical Education
questions.text: In lawn tennis, a match is generally organised into games, which are grouped into
questions.explanation: Tennis matches are structured into games, which are grouped into sets, with a player typically needing to win a set number of sets to win the match.

questions.subject: Physical Education
questions.text: A sudden, complete break in the continuity of a bone is called a
questions.explanation: A fracture describes a break in the continuity of a bone, ranging from a small crack to a complete break.

questions.subject: Physical Education
questions.text: An injury in which a bone is forced out of its normal position at a joint is called a
questions.explanation: A dislocation occurs when a bone is displaced from its normal position within a joint.

questions.subject: Physical Education
questions.text: An injury involving the stretching or tearing of a ligament, typically at a joint, is called a
questions.explanation: A sprain involves the stretching or tearing of a ligament, the connective tissue linking bone to bone at a joint.

questions.subject: Physical Education
questions.text: An injury involving the stretching or tearing of a muscle or tendon is called a
questions.explanation: A strain involves the stretching or tearing of a muscle or tendon, distinct from a sprain which affects ligaments.

questions.subject: Physical Education
questions.text: A painful, involuntary contraction of a muscle, often occurring during or after strenuous exercise, is called a
questions.explanation: A muscle cramp is a sudden, painful, involuntary muscle contraction, often triggered by fatigue, dehydration, or strenuous activity.

questions.subject: Physical Education
questions.text: A head injury resulting from a blow or jolt, potentially causing temporary disruption of brain function, is called a
questions.explanation: A concussion is a traumatic brain injury caused by a blow or jolt to the head, potentially causing temporary disruption of normal brain function.

questions.subject: Physical Education
questions.text: In the RICE protocol for treating minor sports injuries, the 'R' stands for
questions.explanation: The 'R' in the RICE protocol stands for Rest, allowing the injured area time to begin healing without further strain.

questions.subject: Physical Education
questions.text: In the RICE protocol for treating minor sports injuries, the 'I' stands for
questions.explanation: The 'I' in RICE stands for Ice, applied to help reduce swelling and numb pain in the injured area.

questions.subject: Physical Education
questions.text: In the RICE protocol for treating minor sports injuries, the 'C' stands for
questions.explanation: The 'C' in RICE stands for Compression, typically applied using a bandage to help control swelling in the injured area.

questions.subject: Physical Education
questions.text: In the RICE protocol for treating minor sports injuries, the 'E' stands for
questions.explanation: The 'E' in RICE stands for Elevation, raising the injured area above heart level where possible to help reduce swelling.

questions.subject: Physical Education
questions.text: Substances used by athletes to artificially enhance physical performance beyond natural ability are called
questions.explanation: Ergogenic aids refer to substances or methods used to enhance athletic performance, some of which are banned due to health risks or unfair advantage.

questions.subject: Physical Education
questions.text: Synthetic hormones used illegally by some athletes to increase muscle mass and strength are called
questions.explanation: Anabolic steroids are synthetic hormones sometimes misused to artificially increase muscle mass and strength, banned in most competitive sports.

questions.subject: Physical Education
questions.text: A banned performance-enhancement method involving the manipulation of an athlete's blood to increase oxygen-carrying capacity is called
questions.explanation: Blood doping manipulates an athlete's blood (such as through transfusions) to increase red blood cell count and oxygen-carrying capacity, a banned practice in competitive sport.

questions.subject: Physical Education
questions.text: The international body primarily responsible for setting and enforcing anti-doping rules and codes in sport is the
questions.explanation: WADA (World Anti-Doping Agency) is the international body responsible for developing and enforcing anti-doping policies and codes across sports.

questions.subject: Physical Education
questions.text: A tournament format in which a team or player is eliminated after a single loss, continuing until one champion remains, is called
questions.explanation: In a single-elimination (knockout) format, a single loss removes a team or player from the competition, continuing until only one champion remains.

questions.subject: Physical Education
questions.text: A tournament format in which every team or player competes against every other participant, with final standings based on overall results, is called a
questions.explanation: In a league (round-robin) format, every participant competes against every other participant, with rankings determined by overall performance across all matches.

questions.subject: Physical Education
questions.text: Maintaining sports facilities in good condition, including regular inspection and repair, is important mainly to
options: have no bearing on participant experience or safety
eliminate the need for any safety standards
increase the risk of injury to participants intentionally
ensure participant safety and prolong the usable life of the facility
questions.explanation: Regular maintenance of sports facilities helps ensure participant safety and extends the usable life of the equipment and infrastructure.

questions.subject: Physical Education
questions.text: Public relations management in sports administration mainly involves
options: discouraging community interest in sporting events
eliminating the need for any organisational structure
promoting a positive public image and managing communication with stakeholders
avoiding all communication with the public or media
questions.explanation: Public relations management in sports involves promoting a positive image and effectively managing communication with fans, sponsors, media, and other stakeholders.

questions.subject: Physical Education
questions.text: The Nigerian Olympic Committee is primarily responsible for
options: coordinating Nigeria's participation in the Olympic Games and related sports development
questions.explanation: The Nigerian Olympic Committee coordinates the country's participation in the Olympic Games and supports broader national sports development efforts.

questions.subject: Physical Education
questions.text: Effective sports administration generally requires attention to
options: organisation, planning, and coordination of events, facilities, and personnel
avoiding any structured management of sporting activities
eliminating the need for trained officials or personnel
ignoring all aspects of event planning and coordination
questions.explanation: Effective sports administration requires careful organisation, planning, and coordination across events, facilities, and personnel to ensure successful operations.

questions.subject: Physical Education
questions.text: Immediately after a suspected concussion, an athlete should generally be
options: immediately returned to full play with no assessment
given performance-enhancing substances to continue playing
removed from play and assessed by a qualified professional before returning
questions.explanation: An athlete suspected of concussion should be removed from play immediately and properly assessed by a qualified professional before any return to activity.

questions.subject: Physical Education
questions.text: The use of anabolic steroids by athletes carries health risks that can include
options: no effect on the body whatsoever
guaranteed improvement in long-term health with no risks
questions.explanation: Anabolic steroid misuse carries serious health risks, including hormonal imbalances, cardiovascular problems, and other long-term harm.

questions.subject: Physical Education
questions.text: A double-elimination tournament format differs from a single-elimination format mainly in that competitors
options: never face elimination under any circumstances
are eliminated only after two losses, rather than just one
are eliminated immediately after their first loss, same as single-elimination
compete only once throughout the entire tournament
questions.explanation: In a double-elimination format, a competitor must lose twice before being eliminated, offering a second chance not available in single-elimination formats.
